findings.rootCause:
PackedPlanCache.sameSource() accepted a routing-hash candidate as the cached query as soon as snapshot.equals(candidate) was true, before consulting the collision-proof packed identity; the routing fingerprint hashes only class names/var names, and the model equals/hashCode of ArbitraryLengthPath ignored minLength and of GroupConcat ignored the separator. So ?s

* ?o and ?s

+ ?o (and GROUP_CONCAT ',' vs '|') authenticated as the same query and the cached PackedQuery (which does encode minLength/separator) was replayed -> wrong results. (Critique narrative correction adopted: the identity was non-null for these queries because the parser marks constant Vars anonymous; the ordering was the defect.)
findings.change: (A) Model: ArbitraryLengthPath.equals compares minLength and hashCode mixes Long.hashCode(minLength); GroupConcat.equals compares the separator with Objects.equals and hashCode mixes Objects.hashCode(separator). (B) Cache: PackedQueryCacheIdentity.create (nullable) removed; PackedCascadesPlanner.optimizeWithCache and the two-arg PackedPlanCache overloads use createPlanIdentity (non-null for codec-supported algebra, canonicalizes only provably safe anonymous names). sameSource now: mixed (one identity, one none) -> false; known identity mismatch -> false (the load-bearing gate, independent of any future lossy equals); then structural equals confirms; identity match without equals is reused only under the existing alpha-equivalence guard (no external bindings, parameterVariant 0); both-null identities fall back to equals alone (documented: only UNSUPPORTED-codec algebra, which materialization rejects). Family reuse across constants remains legitimate and re-materializes the requested constant (test familyReuseAcrossConstantsMaterializesTheRequestedConstant); the ordering is pinned by identityMismatchRejectsEqualLookingSource with non-null identities on both sides and a deliberately lossy equals under a forced fingerprint collision.

findings.rootCause: (a) PackedPlanCache.Flight.matches let a family waiter join a flight when PackedQueryFamilyIdentity.matches was true. That check compares only the parameter schema and a canonical identity computed WITHOUT range facts. PlanEntry.familyMatches additionally required hasSameCacheIdentity on the concrete query. A query template encoded with a range provider was therefore served to providerless planning (LMDB dirty transactions, version 0), which produced an EmptySet proof for uncommitted rows.

findings.rootCause: PackedPlanCache.FlightClaim.await returned flight.result.join() with no timeout. A failed owner (Segment.fail completes the future exceptionally) therefore reached every waiter as a CompletionException. LmdbCascadesOptimizer.optimizeWithResult caught only IllegalStateException, so the owner's query fell back while each waiter's query failed. UnsupportedCascadesOperatorException (a CascadesPlanningException, not an IllegalStateException) was raised only by PackedPlanMaterializer after the complete search. LmdbPipelinePlanCache waiters called shared.join() after abandon() had completed the owner's future exceptionally.
findings.change: (1) FlightClaim.await returns null on CompletionException, CancellationException, ExecutionException or TimeoutException. The wait is bounded by the flight's planningLimits.deadlineNanos (getNow once the deadline has passed). An interrupt restores the interrupt flag and throws IllegalStateException. (2) PackedCascadesPlanner.optimizeWithCache loops. A cache hit returns the cached result and ownership plans. When await returns null the request re-enters beginFlight once, to take ownership or pick up a published plan. A second abandoned flight, or an owner still blocked at the deadline, leads to a cache-less optimize that publishes nothing, following the critique's 'at most twice' rule. (3) encodeSupportedForPlanning/requireSupported reject PackedRelOp.UNSUPPORTED at all four encode sites before any cost session opens. (4) LmdbCascadesOptimizer catches RuntimeException and unwraps CompletionException. It rethrows QueryInterruptedException and any failure seen while the thread is interrupted. Under -ea it asserts that the input tree still equals the pre-search clone. It logs WARN and counts fallbacks in cascadesFallbackCount(). (5) LmdbPipelinePlanCache waiters catch CompletionException/CancellationException from shared.join() and compute their own plan without publishing. bR added a coverage test for the critique's cancellation rule (planningFailureWhileInterruptedAbortsInsteadOfFallingBack). b2's catch already implements that rule, so the test was green on first run. It guards against the widened catch swallowing a cancellation.

findings.rootCause: LmdbEstimatorRuntime.snapshotVersion() = max(TripleStore.getDataRevision(), synopsis.snapshotVersion()). The data revision was an in-memory AtomicLong that restarted at 0 and incremented once per commit, while the synopsis version is persisted. After a restart with persisted synopsis version V, the cache data identity therefore stayed at V for the first V commits, and cached EmptySet proofs and anchored plans kept being served.
findings.change: TripleStore: dataRevision is now the LMDB transaction id of the committing write txn, captured before mdb_txn_commit frees the handle. At open it is seeded from a read txn's mdb_txn_id. publishDataRevision = max(current+1, txnId), so the revision is durable, monotonic across restarts and advances on every commit. It is still published AFTER txnManager.reset(). The critique suggested bumping it before the reset, but a planner that sees the new revision while pooled readers still show old data would then key old data under the new revision, persistently. The kept order leaves only the transient 3.5/3.10 window, which the before/after revision checks in the caches close. LmdbEstimatorRuntime.snapshotVersion() returns the data revision alone. frontierPlanningRevision() mixes in the synopsis version, so a synopsis publish still refreshes plans on the evidence side.

findings.rootCause: LmdbFilterSelectivityStats keyed both exact-probe caches (bounded zero proofs and COMPLETE stored-term enumerations) on currentSnapshotIdentity(). With the sketch estimator on, that identity is the sketch synopsis identity, which moves only when a background rebuild publishes. Otherwise it is the statement mutation stamp, which does not move while Frontier is OFF. reset() never cleared the caches. A pre-commit COMPLETE term set therefore became an exact VALUES anchor for later planning, and committed value-equal rows were lost.
findings.change: probeSnapshotIdentity() = SketchSnapshotIdentity(0, 0, tripleStore.getDataRevision()) keys both probe caches and snapshotStillCurrent. currentSnapshotIdentity() keeps its sidecar/synopsis role; the critique confirmed that all its other users are sidecar semantics. LmdbSnapshotProbeCache gained clear(), and reset() now clears both caches. bR simplification (Routine B): removed a try/catch(RuntimeException) -> null around getDataRevision(), a plain AtomicLong read that cannot throw. It would only have hidden errors as silently skipped caching. Pre-green and post-green come from the same classes. The critique asked for isExactBoundedFilterZero to re-probe after the data revision moves while the sketch identity stays unchanged: LmdbExactFilterProbeCacheTest#dataRevisionInvalidatesExactProbe (renamed from mutationVersionInvalidatesExactProbe) and LmdbExactProbeCacheDataRevisionTest#sketchIdentityChangeAloneDoesNotClearProbes cover that path, which LmdbStorageEstimatorEvidence.exactBoundedFilterZero uses.

findings.rootCause: The LMDB pipeline's request-bound rewrites embed committed-store facts before Cascades runs: LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer.exactStoredTermFilterAnchor replaces FILTER(?o = c) with a VALUES anchor enumerating the COMPLETE committed stored terms value-equal to c (true only for the planning data revision), and materializedSmallLiteralFilterAnchor drops/exactifies the filter on the strength of the predicate's object-domain guarantee (true only while that guarantee keeps its contents). LmdbPipelinePlanCache.publishDecision stripped the only hard identity (PredicateRangeIdentity) unless the PACKED summary declared PREDICATE_RANGE_DATA (a packed rule proof; pipeline rewrites never set it) and the data revision existed only in the soft EvidenceSnapshot, so LmdbPlanDecisionCache.lookupVersion answered UseAndRefresh('outside-stability-envelope') after any commit and served the anchored plan; LmdbDetachedPlanRefresh replanned the already-rewritten prepared source (anchor included) and its ensureSemanticsCurrent compared only predicateRangeVersion, a schema hash (encoding + exclusion config + flags) that no commit changes, so the refresh republished the stale anchor permanently. Two latent gaps found by the critique made a naive hard dependency unusable: (a) SemanticDependencies had one index dimension (indexGeneration/indexIdentity) so a contents-only tier could not coexist with a data-revision tier on lookup; (b) publishBuild refuses to replace a VALID family version and nothing marked HARD_INVALID on a mismatch (hardInvalid only via markEvidenceChanged, no production caller), so a hard mismatch would replan on every invocation forever.
findings.change: Roadmap 4.2 rewrite certificates, scoped to the caches. (1) New LmdbPlanAssumptions record (committedSnapshotDependent, guaranteePredicates) with dedicated planned metrics optimizer.planAssumption.committedSnapshot / optimizer.planAssumption.guaranteePredicate; LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer stamps the first exactly at the exact stored-term anchor (:455) and the second only where a guarantee decided the drop/expansion (consumedGuaranteePredicate mirrors canMaterializeSmallLiteralFilterAnchor/expandFiniteAnchor; the OPTIONAL safe-values shortcut with nothing to expand is not stamped), never derived from OPTIMIZER_GUARANTEE_ANCHOR_PREDICATE (critique minor). LmdbQueryOptimizerPipeline.computePlan collects the assumptions from the pre-Cascades tree (PackedPlanMaterializer does not carry source metrics), annotates the plan (optimizer.planAssumptions, explain-visible) and passes them into PlanComputation and LmdbDetachedPlanRefresh. (2) Two-tier hard dependencies (critique major #1): SemanticDependencies gains dataRevision/dataRevisionDependent next to indexGeneration/indexIdentity/indexGenerationDependent; the lookup side always supplies both (semanticDependencies(context) with dataRevision = planning data revision, dependent=true, identity = PredicateRangeIdentity); publishDecision narrows per assumptions via hardDependencies(): committedSnapshot -> keep the data-revision tier (any commit -> replan), guarantee-dependent (assumption or packed PREDICATE_RANGE_DATA) -> keep the identity tier (contents-only, indexGeneration 0L as before, commits that leave the guarantee unchanged still USE/USE_AND_REFRESH), neither -> both stripped (today's use-and-refresh). matchesCurrent compares only the declared tiers. RefreshComputation/RefreshPublication/publishRefresh mirror the fields so refreshed versions keep the hard dependency. (3) Publication after a mismatch (critique major #2): lookupVersion CASes the family version to hardInvalid (and re-points aliases) before returning replan('semantic-dependency-mismatch'), so publishBuild accepts the plan built for the current dependencies and the third run is a cache hit (asserted e2e: afterCommitPlan pipelinePlanCacheHit=true, USE). (4) LmdbDetachedPlanRefresh carries the assumptions, the build data revision and the build PredicateRangeIdentity; ensureAssumptionsCurrent refuses (before opening a planning snapshot, and again after planning) when committedSnapshotDependent && dataRevision != build revision or when a consumed guarantee's identity changed; predicateRangeDependent = packed summary || guarantee assumption; the refreshed FamilyVersion keeps the same hard tiers. (5) predicateRangeVersion is documented as the guarantee SCHEMA version (LmdbEstimatorStorageAccess, TripleStore.effectiveRdfTermDomainsVersion); guarantee CONTENTS are keyed through PredicateRangeIdentity (pipeline decision cache) and, for the packed cache, through Context.dataRevision (a contents change is a commit) plus b2's sameQueryContext predicateRangeVersion check. Commit-visibility vs revision-bump ordering (critique blocker for this batch): analysed and documented in LmdbPipelinePlanCache.getOrComputePlan -- the pipeline captures context.revision() before planning and publishes only if it equals the revision re-read after planning; the exact-probe caches (b2) and LmdbDetachedPlanRefresh bracket their reads the same way; with TripleStore publishing the revision only after the readers were reset (b2), a plan/probe can never be keyed under a revision newer than the data it enumerated, and the residual 'newer data under the captured revision' case is either caught by the re-check or keyed under a revision no later lookup uses. Deviation from the task wording, following the design: the detached refresh still starts from the prepared (rewritten) source; re-running the request-bound optimizers inside the detached refresh would require it to retain the pipeline/estimator/strategy it is contractually forbidden to retain and is a plan-quality item, not a correctness one, once a refresh cannot run on stale assumptions (detachedRefreshMustNotReplanFromStaleAnchoredPreparedSource is green: the refresh is refused and the synchronous replan re-runs the rewrites against current data). bR: removed the leftover debug report() helper, which printed every plan to stdout, from LmdbPlanCacheCommitInvalidationTest. The explain calls it wrapped are kept, so lookup behavior is unchanged. The class was green again afterwards (10/0/0, log .mvnf/workspaces/wp3/logs/20260928T070733.228183Z-37543-5cb64cb3/verify.log) and in the full lmdb suite (log .mvnf/workspaces/wp3/logs/20260928T072152.064036Z-43479-eddb2b11/verify.log).

crossWpNotes: Critique reconciliation (every item checked against the code): [major 3.3.2 two-tier] handled: SemanticDependencies has dataRevision/dataRevisionDependent next to indexIdentity/indexGenerationDependent, and matchesCurrent compares only the declared tiers (LmdbPlanDecisionCache); tests LmdbPipelinePlanCacheAssumptionTest#guaranteeAssumptionIsReusedAtANewDataRevisionWhenIdentityUnchanged and LmdbPlanCacheCommitInvalidationTest#guaranteeOnlyPlanIsReusedWhileTheGuaranteeHoldsAndReplansWhenItBreaks. [major 3.3.2 publication] handled: lookupVersion hard-invalidates the version on a semantic mismatch, so publishBuild can replace it. It is reached only through lookupExact, whose key already pins every request-shaped dimension, so only store-state changes retire versions. Tests: LmdbPlanDecisionCacheHardDependencyTest#hardDependencyMismatchAllowsReplacementBuild, and e2e exactStoredTermAnchorMustNotSurviveCommitThatAddsValueEqualTerm asserts pipelinePlanCacheHit=true and USE after the replan. [minor 3.8.4 cancellation] handled in LmdbCascadesOptimizer, plus a new bR guard test. [minor 3.3.1 narrative/ordering] handled: identity mismatch rejects before equals (identityMismatchRejectsEqualLookingSource). [minor 3.3.2 stamps] handled: dedicated metrics only where the guarantee decided, collected pre-Cascades. [minor 3.3.3 ordering] addressed by deliberate deviation (see ordering note). [minor 3.9.1 {null}] documented as restricted-dataset semantics, consistent with datasetUsesStoreDefaults, and pinned e2e. [minor 3.8.4 loop-twice] handled: waiterFallsBackToIndependentPlanningWhenTwoOwnersFail. [minor 3.3.4 bounded-zero re-probe] handled: LmdbExactFilterProbeCacheTest#dataRevisionInvalidatesExactProbe. [missed findings] publication authority and two dimensions are the majors above; the ordering is documented; annotateCertifiedExactZero was verified to have no correctness consumer (see followUps).

wp1: every new LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer anchor or drop path that consumes committed stored terms or a predicate guarantee must call LmdbPlanAssumptions.stampCommittedSnapshot / stampGuaranteePredicate. Otherwise the pipeline decision cache uses and refreshes the plan across commits.

wp2/wp7: a packed proof that consumes an exact committed-data fact must declare a PackedPlanDecisionSummary semantic dependency that LmdbPipelinePlanCache.hardDependencies maps to the data-revision tier. PREDICATE_RANGE_DATA maps to the guarantee-identity tier.

wp7: PackedFrontierSubsetKernelContractTest#arbitraryWidthBushyDependentJoinContinuesRightRecipeUnderWholeLeftPrefix needs about 104-113 s of its 120 s preemptive budget and times out on a loaded host in every worktree. It needs a planner speedup or a budget review.

wp5: flaky IOException 'Frontier mutation journal no longer retains all mutations after sequence N' from TripleStore.readFrontierMutationsAfter (seen once in b3 in LmdbPlanCacheCommitInvalidationTest#snapshotTransactionMustNotUseAnchorsProbedFromNewerCommit; green in every run since).

3.3.3/3.5 ordering: TripleStore publishes the data revision AFTER txnManager.reset(), deliberately. Together with the before/after revision checks in LmdbPipelinePlanCache and LmdbDetachedPlanRefresh, this means old data can never be keyed under a new revision. Moving the bump before the reset (the critique's suggestion) would reintroduce persistent poisoning.

Integrator: core/sail/lmdb/.lwjgl/ (native libs extracted by the test runtime) is left untracked and excluded from wp3.patch. Earlier wp3 patches contained it as undiffable 'Binary files differ' hunks, which break git apply. Consider adding core/sail/lmdb/.lwjgl/ to .gitignore next to /tools/server/.lwjgl/.

The behavior is covered in the evaluation module by PackedPlanningFailSafeTest#waiterReplansAndSucceedsWhenTheOwnerFails (injected failing cost model) and in LMDB by LmdbPipelinePlanCacheFailedFlightTest.

Verified missed finding (critique): annotateCertifiedExactZero stamps PLANNED_CARDINALITY_ROWS=0 on the plan root only. Its sole runtime consumer is JoinQueryEvaluationStep.RuntimeEstimate (a bound-statement-guard heuristic), with no short-circuit on a planned zero. A stale zero can therefore cost performance but never rows.
